pr_title: bluetooth: smp: Add authentication callbacks per connection
pr_body:
Change introduces authentication callbacks used only for specified BLE connection. The feature can be used by devices that require reporting specific bonding capabilities only when pairing using vendor-specific procedures.

If per-connection authentication callbacks are defined for given connection, they are used instead of global authentication
callbacks. SMP latches authentication callbacks during the first access to prevent updating the callbacks while pairing.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38336

Signed-off-by: Marek Pieta <Marek.Pieta@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments:
> Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38336

That doesn't seem right - The issue is about auth-per-identity. This PR seems to be auth-per-connection, which is not the same.

@Thalley, I already discussed it with @kapi-no who reported the issue. He informed me that newly introduced API is fine for him and as soon as this will go in, he can close the issue.

His application could check the local identity used for newly established connection and simply assign proper set of callbacks for that connection using new API. This approach is more generic, assigning callbacks per local identity would not work in Fast Pair use-case.

> > Fixes: #38336
> 
> That doesn't seem right - The issue is about auth-per-identity. This PR seems to be auth-per-connection, which is not the same.

Yes, we have discussed it with @MarekPieta. This PR does not implement my suggestion in the exact form that was described in the #38336 issue. However, the current solution satisfies my requirements and is even more flexible. If we merge this feature, I would consider my issue fixed.

Hi @jhedberg, @Vudentz, @sjanc, @alwa-nordic 
Could you review, please?

> I'm still not completely convinced that this is the best approach, e.g. the chance of race conditions with the registering and an authentication procedure starting before that makes it feel like maybe there's some better way to do this.
> 
> Anyway, assuming we go forward with this, please take a look at the couple of inline comments I had. Thanks.

Hi @jhedberg
I don't intend to force approach suggested by me in this PR and I am open for discussion. I would be glad to discuss other possible solutions for my original issue. On my end the update is needed for Fast Pair use-case, I make sure to introduce approach that would fix other related use-cases (new API also fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38336).

I fully understand that in general updating callbacks after connection is established may introduce risk of races. Since Fast Pair specification actually requires changing bonding capabilities reacting on GATT write (that's the moment when we are aware that we should follow the procedure for a given connection), we cannot completely avoid possibility of race here (e.g. we cannot guarantee that connected Central would not behave improperly). I used atomic pointer to avoid unexpected behaviors and clearly indicate problem to the end user (no better solution comes to my mind, but maybe I missed something).

Maybe we should have additional pointer in smp for currently used auth_cb,   on start of pair it would be set either from conn or global and use during that pairing. That should solve all the races (including  global auth cb change)

> Maybe we should have additional pointer in smp for currently used auth_cb, on start of pair it would be set either from conn or global and use during that pairing. That should solve all the races (including global auth cb change)

Hi @sjanc
Actually we already have it (such atomic pointer defined per smp instance is introduced as part of this PR) :)
There is still possibility of "race" between assigning per-connection auth callbacks and start of SMP procedure (in general we cannot synchronize them, so I decided to use atomic pointer and return error code to clearly indicate that the SMP procedure already started and we cannot update auth callbacks for given connection so that the procedure would rely on global set of callbacks)
@jhedberg, the changes are pushed. Please rereview

> > Maybe we should have additional pointer in smp for currently used auth_cb, on start of pair it would be set either from conn or global and use during that pairing. That should solve all the races (including global auth cb change)
> 
> Hi @sjanc Actually we already have it (such atomic pointer defined per smp instance is introduced as part of this PR) :) There is still possibility of "race" between assigning per-connection auth callbacks and start of SMP procedure (in general we cannot synchronize them, so I decided to use atomic pointer and return error code to clearly indicate that the SMP procedure already started and we cannot update auth callbacks for given connection so that the procedure would rely on global set of callbacks)

@sjanc are you ok with the above explanation, or did you mean something else?
@jhedberg, I applied changes requested so far. Please rereview

> @jhedberg, I applied changes requested so far.

I've seen, thanks. As I mentioned in my earlier comment, I'm waiting for some ack/nack from @sjanc before approving/merging.

Hi @Thalley
I added release note and rebased on main. Please rereview
Force pushed to retrigger CI tests

> Force pushed to retrigger CI tests

Since this resets all approvals, this isn't the best way of doing it. You can restart a CI test without pushing the PR again :)

I would like to note that this API smells a bit of race condition. It can only be used after a connection is established, but before the remote initiates an SMP procedure. This can, for now, be done safely in `bt_conn_cb.connected`. But that's because of hidden/undocumented thread-priority reasons.

Is it correct that the intended use of this new API is to select the pairing method? Would it work to instead extend `struct bt_conn_auth_cb` with a `.select_pairing_method(bt_conn, bt_conn_pairing_feat)` that can downgrade `smp_pairing_req`:`rsp->io_capability`?

> Is it correct that the intended use of this new API is to select the pairing method?

That is actually a good question. This PR fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38336, but the issue that is being fixed only states that this should be possible, but does not give any use cases or reasons for it (which is also lacking in the PR description).

> I was rather thinking on having one ptr in struct bt_conn and one in struct bt_smp then when pairing starts we could have: if (conn->auth_cb) { smp->auth_cb = conn->auth_cb; } else { smp->auth_cb = global_smp_auth; }
> 
> That way smp->auth_cb will not be change during pairing regardless if global or connection callbacks are altered

Hi @sjanc
Implementation provided in the PR already ensures that authentication callbacks used for given connection are not altered during pairing. The only difference is that my proposed API assigns callbacks directly to SMP and returns error code if it's no longer possible (e.g. because SMP procedures have already started). Assigning the callbacks to connection slightly increases memory consumption and it does not improve anything (it may even lead to new race conditions, because authentication callbacks would then be stored in two places and copied between them). With implementation proposed in the PR, I could use atomic pointer as a very simple synchronization too.

Hi @alwa-nordic 

> I would like to note that this API smells a bit of race condition. It can only be used after a connection is established, but before the remote initiates an SMP procedure. This can, for now, be done safely in `bt_conn_cb.connected`. But that's because of hidden/undocumented thread-priority reasons.

The race condition is in theory possible, but the vendor-specific procedure must be triggered before device receives SMP request anyway (otherwise device is unaware that it should use vendor-specific procedure instead of regular pairing and cannot react properly no matter which implementation is used). Also in the worst case (e.g. if peer actually starts SMP before informing that it's going to follow vendor-specific procedure) device would try to follow default pairing procedure which would still be correct behavior.

> Is it correct that the intended use of this new API is to select the pairing method? Would it work to instead extend `struct bt_conn_auth_cb` with a `.select_pairing_method(bt_conn, bt_conn_pairing_feat)` that can downgrade `smp_pairing_req`:`rsp->io_capability`?

If we would like to modify device's behavior during pairing, we would need to modify other authentications callbacks anyway, so I think that the additional callback is not enough here. The whole pairing flow is modified, it's not only about the IO capabilities. Also if we report given set of IO capabilities, we would need to ensure that we provide needed authentication callbacks (currently IO capabilities are reported relying on used set of authentication callbacks which prevents errors here).

Hi @Thalley

> > Is it correct that the intended use of this new API is to select the pairing method?
> 
> That is actually a good question. This PR fixes #38336, but the issue that is being fixed only states that this should be possible, but does not give any use cases or reasons for it (which is also lacking in the PR description).

Since feature introduced by this PR could be used for various use-cases, I added only a short, generic description in the PR and commit message:
`Change introduces authentication callbacks used only for specified BLE connection. The feature can be used by devices that require reporting specific bonding capabilities only when pairing using vendor-specific procedures.`

**Fast Pair use-case**
Since this use-case was discussed in details during review of my previously proposed solution which was a separate PR (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/46637), I provide short description of Fast Pair use-case below:

```
An example of use-case is bonding using Fast Pair. In that case Central triggers vendor-specific BLE bonding procedure using GATT write to predefined characteristic before sending SMP request. Then devices use Numeric Comparison pairing method to achieve MITM protection. The only exception is the fact that encrypted passkeys are exchanged by devices over GATT instead of displaying them and waiting for user input. If Central does not trigger the vendor-specific BLE bonding procedure, regular pairing is used.
```
For additional details, see Fast Pair specification: https://developers.google.com/nearby/fast-pair/specifications/service/gatt

** Solved issue **
For https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38336, the new API can be used to override the authentication callbacks right after connection is established for a given Bluetooth local identity (on connected callback). That was already discussed with @kapi-no.
Rebased onto main to fix CI issues (the issues were not directly related to the introduced changes).

Hi @sjanc, @Thalley, @alwa-nordic, @jhedberg
Please take a second look. It would be great if we could merge this feature as soon as possible.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: separate authentication callbacks for each identity
issue_context.body:
Currently, the user can register only one instance of authentication callbacks using the ```bt_conn_auth_cb_register``` API. These callbacks determine globally the pairing flow and the chosen pairing method (Just Works, Numeric Comparison, etc.). As a result, each Bluetooth identity can pair according to the global configuration of authentication callbacks.

It should be possible to configure authentication callbacks separately for each Bluetooth identity.

Use case: The first identity for Bluetooth application with higher security requirements needs to do authenticated pairing (e.g. Numeric Comparison). The second identity has lower security requirements. Just Works pairing is sufficient for it.

If we don't want to break existing APIs and the behaviour of the current Bluetooth stack, we can create another version of the ```bt_conn_auth_cb_register``` API which takes Bluetooth identity index as an additional parameter. During the pairing process, we can use the authentication callback configuration for a given identity if it is registered. If it is not registered, then we will use the global configuration to control the pairing process.

review_comments: Is it possible to make `struct bt_smp *smp` const ?
Unfortunately not, because `get_auth_cb` performs `atomic_ptr_cas` on `smp->auth_cb` (needed for multi-context safety).
Suggest to use `CHECKKIF` for static checks like these that can always be verified by the caller before calling

`bt_conn_auth_cb_register` in Zephyr validates the authentication callbacks before they are registered in the same way. I think that caller's input validation is fine and it does not introduce significant performance overhead. Can we leave it as it is?
We can leave it as is - Was just a suggestion :)

We can add more description to this API documentation:

_It is recommended to overlay globally defined callbacks (see @ref bt_conn_auth_cb_register) in the context of the connected callback. Following this recommendation guarantees that the override is successful. Suppose the user chooses to override authentication callbacks at the later stage of the connection session. In that case, they risk failure for this API call because security procedures in the SMP module might have already started._

This recommendation assumes that the SMP instance is available and initialized at this point. This is probably true because it is initialized in the L2CAP connected callback context. @MarekPieta, please verify if you haven't analyzed it already

The `bt_conn_connected` defined in `host/conn.c` seems to call `bt_l2cap_connected` before `notify_connected`. Because of that the registered connection callbacks should be called after l2cap channels are notified about the connection. So that SMP should be initialized before user is notified about a new connection.

I updated API doc informing about the mentioned root causes of returning error code.
I would not suggest that the callbacks must be updated in the connected callbacks. This could actually be done at any point until the per-connection callbacks are already assigned or security procedures in the SMP module have already started.
I'm not sure I follow this. `BT_SMP_AUTH_CB_UNINITIALIZED` seems to be used to compare `smp->auth_cb`, but those are different structs. Why are we using this for comparison?

The value of `NULL` cannot be used to signalize that authentication callbacks are not initialized, because it denotes that application provided no callbacks (value of `NULL` is provided by application to signalize it has no bonding capabilities).
I needed a memory address that would never be occupied by the application's authentication callbacks and decided to arbitrary use address of bt_smp_pool for that purpose.

So you just needed a non-NULL, non-valid pointer to denote that the conn-specific auth CB was not initialized?

It seems like kind of a hack (even if documented properly). Wonder if it's worth to allocate another atomic variable for this specific reason instead.

I would prefer to keep it as it is. I understand it could look hacky, but even if we allocate a dedicated variable, the types still would not match (and we would need some additional memory for the variable).
Keep in mind that pointing to SMP's internal data should be safe in this use-case.
